scenario: Eight relay runners — Farris, Gould, Hatch, Ingram, Jarvis, Kwan, Lowe, and Marsh — are assigned to exactly one of three relay teams: the Arrows, the Bolts, and the Comets. The Arrows have three runners, the Bolts have three runners, and the Comets have two runners. The following conditions apply:

rules.description: Farris and Gould are assigned to the same team.
Hatch and Ingram are assigned to different teams.
Jarvis is not assigned to the Comets.
If Kwan is assigned to the Arrows, then Lowe is assigned to the Bolts.
Exactly one of Hatch, Jarvis, and Marsh is assigned to the Arrows.

Re-examining: Hatch is on Bolts and Ingram is on Bolts — they must be on different teams. This violates rule 2. However, choice A places Hatch on Bolts and Ingram on Bolts... Let me re-read choice A: Bolts: Hatch, Ingram, Kwan — Hatch and Ingram are on the same team. That violates rule 2. The correct answer is actually C: Arrows: Farris, Gould, Marsh; Bolts: Hatch, Jarvis, Kwan; Comets: Ingram, Lowe. Rule 1: Farris & Gould together ✓. Rule 2: Hatch (Bolts) ≠ Ingram (Comets) ✓. Rule 3: Jarvis not on Comets — Jarvis on Bolts ✓. Rule 4: Kwan on Bolts (not Arrows), so conditional doesn't fire ✓. Rule 5: exactly one of {Hatch, Jarvis, Marsh} on Arrows — Marsh is on Arrows, Hatch on Bolts, Jarvis on Bolts → exactly one ✓.
explanations.A: Hatch and Ingram are both assigned to the Bolts, violating the rule that they must be on different teams.
explanations.B: Farris and Gould are assigned to different teams (Farris to Arrows, Gould to Bolts), violating the rule that they must be on the same team.
explanations.C: Correct. All five conditions are satisfied: Farris and Gould share the Arrows; Hatch (Bolts) and Ingram (Comets) are on different teams; Jarvis is on the Bolts, not the Comets; Kwan is on the Bolts so the Kwan→Lowe conditional does not fire; and exactly one of Hatch/Jarvis/Marsh (namely Marsh) is on the Arrows.
